Significance: First among the 12 Jyotirlingas, situated on the western coast.
Symbolizes protection from poison and evil, near coastal Dwarka.
Only south-facing (Dakshinamukhi) Jyotirlinga, Lord of Time.
Located on an island shaped like the sacred Om on the Narmada River.
Source of the Bhima River, nestled in the Sahyadri Hills.
Source of the Godavari River; three-faced lingam representing Trimurti.
Last of the 12 Jyotirlingas, located near the UNESCO Ellora Caves.
Set in Nallamala Hills; both a Jyotirlinga and a Shakti Peetha.
Southernmost Jyotirlinga, established by Lord Rama before crossing to Lanka.
Located in the holy city of Varanasi on the banks of the Ganges.
Known as the wish-fulfilling Kamna Linga and healing shrine.
Highest altitude Jyotirlinga in the Garhwal Himalayas; open May–October.
